Large Cap Fund.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in shares of the 100 largest listed companies; the rest can be in other shares, debt and cash.

Large & Mid Cap Fund.mayHold: At least 35% in large companies and at least 35% in mid-sized companies, with the rest anywhere.

Mid Cap Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares of mid-sized companies; the rest can be in other shares, debt and cash.

Small Cap Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares of smaller companies; the rest can be in other shares, debt and cash.

Multi Cap Fund.mayHold: At least 25% each in large, mid-sized and smaller companies, and at least 75% in shares overall.

Flexi Cap Fund.mayHold: Shares of companies of any size, at least 65% of the money; the rest can be in debt and cash.

Focused Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares, spread over no more than 30 companies.

Value Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares picked using a value approach, which looks for shares priced low against the company's worth.

Contra Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares, chosen to go against the current market trend.

Dividend Yield Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares of companies that pay higher dividends.

Sectoral/Thematic Fund.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in shares of one sector or theme, such as banks or technology.

ELSS.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in shares of companies of any size; money is locked in for three years by law.

Index Fund.mayHold: Shares that make up a market index, in the same proportion as the index; the fund copies the index rather than choosing companies.

Aggressive Hybrid Fund.mayHold: Between 65% and 80% of the money in shares and the rest in debt; the mix can change within those limits.

Conservative Hybrid Fund.mayHold: Between 10% and 25% of the money in shares and the rest mostly in debt.

Balanced Advantage Fund.mayHold: A changing mix of shares and debt, where the share of each moves with market conditions.

Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund.mayHold: A changing mix of shares and debt, where the share of each moves with market conditions.

Multi Asset Allocation Fund.mayHold: At least 10% each in three asset types, usually shares, debt and gold.

Arbitrage Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in shares, offset by opposite trades in the futures market, with the rest in debt.

Equity Savings Fund.mayHold: A mix of shares, offsetting futures trades and debt, with at least 65% in shares counting the offsetting trades.

Liquid Fund.mayHold: Debt papers that return the money within 91 days; it holds no shares.

Overnight Fund.mayHold: Debt papers that return the money the next day; it holds no shares.

Ultra Short Duration Fund.mayHold: Bonds and other debt papers that return the money in three to six months; it holds no shares.

Low Duration Fund.mayHold: Bonds and other debt papers that return the money in six to twelve months; it holds no shares.

Short Duration Fund.mayHold: Bonds and other debt papers that return the money in one to three years; it holds no shares.

Medium Duration Fund.mayHold: Bonds and other debt papers that return the money in three to four years; it holds no shares.

Long Duration Fund.mayHold: Bonds and other debt papers that return the money in more than seven years; it holds no shares.

Corporate Bond Fund.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in highly rated company bonds; it holds no shares.

Banking and PSU Fund.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in debt papers of banks, public sector companies and public financial institutions.

Gilt Fund.mayHold: At least 80% of the money in government bonds; it holds no shares.

Money Market Fund.mayHold: Debt papers that return the money within one year; it holds no shares.

Credit Risk Fund.mayHold: At least 65% of the money in lower-rated company bonds; it holds no shares.
